Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matched frame cap gives a smooth, tear-free experience that suits this slower-paced strategy game; medium terrain and water quality keep the map attractive while shadows are kept low to ease CPU/GPU load. This is the sweet spot for most play sessions.
Optimal.ExpectedFps: 38-42 fps (early/mid game stable; late game may dip to 30)

profiles.Summary: Crusader Kings III is a grand strategy / simulation game with modest GPU demands — its bottleneck on the Steam Deck is the CPU handling complex AI calculations rather than rendering, so frame rates are generally stable but can dip during late-game with large maps and many AI rulers. The game runs well under Proton and is Steam Deck Verified (Playable), with UI scaling and mouse-only support making it reasonably comfortable on the small screen.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements, the Deck's hardware capabilities, and the game's known CPU-heavy grand strategy nature. On your first session, check the frame rate during a late-game year with many active rulers — if it dips below your cap regularly, drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile and reduce the Graphics Quality preset one step.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 7 W TDP and a reduced render resolution, the GPU is barely stressed and battery life is maximised; the CPU remains the limiting factor in late-game, so the 30 fps cap prevents fruitless GPU overwork. FSR upscaling from 960x600 keeps the map readable.
MaxBattery.ExpectedFps: 30 fps (stable early game, occasional dips to 25 in late game)

KnownIssues: UI and text can be small on the 1280x800 screen despite the game's adjustable text size option; zooming in on the map is often necessary.
Late-game AI processing can cause noticeable frame dips and longer turn/pause cycles as the number of rulers and events grows.
No native controller layout — the game is mouse-driven, so a community trackpad layout or mouse-mode is required for comfortable play.
Occasional Proton compatibility quirks reported (gold/trending gold tier); some players report needing to verify game files after updates.

MaxPerformance.Notes: CK3's GPU demands are modest enough that native 1280x800 at High settings is achievable early in a campaign; the real ceiling is CPU throughput for AI, so expect frame rate to soften in complex late-game situations regardless of GPU settings. Motion blur is disabled as it adds no value on a handheld screen.
MaxPerformance.ExpectedFps: 50-60 fps (early game); 35-45 fps (late game with many rulers)

Optimal.Notes: Medium settings at native resolution look sharp and detailed on the OLED screen, and the game's CPU-bound nature means the GPU has headroom to spare. Increase text size in accessibility settings to improve readability on the small display.
Optimal.ExpectedFps: 55-60 fps (may dip to 45 in late game)

profiles.Summary: Crusader Kings III is a grand strategy game that is largely CPU-bound and light on GPU demands, making it well-suited to the Steam Deck's hardware despite its "Playable" Verified rating. The game runs comfortably at 60 fps on medium settings and can stretch to 90 fps, though late-game with large maps and many AI rulers can cause CPU-driven slowdowns.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and the game's known CPU-bound grand strategy nature. On your first session, check frame rates during a late-game year with many active rulers and wars — if it dips below your cap, the bottleneck is CPU simulation, not GPU, so lowering graphics settings further will not help much.

MaxBattery.Notes: CK3 is primarily CPU-bound, so reducing GPU load via low settings and a modest TDP limit yields excellent battery life without meaningfully hurting the strategy experience. Late-game simulation complexity may cause dips regardless of GPU settings.

KnownIssues: Small UI text and tooltips can be difficult to read on the 1280x800 screen, though the game does include an Adjustable Text Size feature
Late-game performance may dip as the simulation scales up with more entities, dynasties, and events being processed simultaneously
Mouse-only UI elements and some menus may require touchscreen or trackpad use, as controller support is limited
Proton compatibility is rated Playable (not Verified), meaning some minor interface or input quirks may require workarounds

MaxPerformance.Notes: CK3's GPU requirements are modest enough that high settings are achievable at full TDP, but the CPU simulation becomes the bottleneck in late-game large campaigns; dropping to 60 Hz if frame rate becomes unstable is recommended.
